member.name: T:GrayWolf.Gaze.ConditionalAttribute
member.summary: Base for any attribute that shows, hides, enables or disables a field based on the value of a member bool or a bool-returning function.

remarks.para: A condition may name a serialized field, a property, or a parameterless method returning bool. The member may be private, static, or declared on a base type. Prefix a name with '!' to negate, for example "!useCustomRate".

Resolution starts at the field's own container and walks up to the serialized object root, so a condition inside a nested struct or a list element resolves against its immediate neighbours first. An unresolvable name leaves the field visible and enabled and reports the problem in the inspector rather than throwing.
Supplying an switches from "is this bool true" to "does this member equal that value", which is what allows a condition on an enum or a number.

member.name: M:GrayWolf.Gaze.ContextItem.Reset
member.summary: Resets the object so it can be used as a new instance next time it is created. To avoid memory allocations and generating garbage, the system reuses objects. This function should clear the object so it can be reused without leaking any information (e.g. pointers to objects that will no longer be valid to access). So it is important the implementation carefully clears all relevant members. Note that this is different from a Dispose or Destructor as the object in not freed but reset. This can be useful when havin large sub-allocated objects like arrays or lists which can be cleared and reused without re-allocating.
